reproduction_target: Regeneration of the genomic analyses reported in the paper from raw sequence: Micro-C chromatin interaction analysis in mouse granulosa cells at 0h vs 6h post-hCG (alignment, valid-pair extraction, contact matrices, loop/TAD/A-B-compartment calling), enhancer definition by loop-anchor x TSS x ATAC intersection, motif and TF-occupancy enrichment at enhancer classes, and AR/GR/H3K27ac ChIP-seq peak calling plus differential binding, annotation, GO enrichment and signal heatmaps. Wet-lab animal work, library preparation and sequencing are out of scope.
granularity_note: No workflow file (no Snakefile/Nextflow/CWL/WDL/Makefile) exists because no code repository is stated anywhere in the paper. Steps were therefore derived at one-step-per-named-tool-invocation from the Methods subsections 'Micro-C', 'Enhancer identification', 'ChIP-seq', 'Additional datasets' and 'Statistical analysis'. Two HOMER invocations on different input sets (enhancer classes vs ChIP-seq peaks) are kept as separate steps because their inputs and backgrounds differ. Merge/sort/deduplication of pairs is kept separate from pairtools parse because the paper names parameters only for parse.

steps.label: Micro-C read QC with FastQC (Dovetail Genomics Micro-C pipeline)
Micro-C alignment to mm10 with BWA-MEM, parameters "-5SP-T0"
Valid ligation event identification with pairtools, "parse --min-mapq 40 --walks-policy 5unique --max-inter-align-gap 30"
Merge of technical/biological replicate pairs, sorting and deduplication (tool unnamed)
Multi-resolution contact matrix generation with Juicertools (5-50 kb bins)
Chromatin loop calling with HICCUPS at 5/10/25 kb, default settings
Differential loop identification with HICCUPSdiff
TAD identification with Arrowhead at 5/10/50 kb, default parameters
A/B compartment calling with CALDER at 25 kb, default parameters
mm10 TSS coordinate retrieval via biomaRt
Loop-anchor x TSS overlap with ChIPpeakAnno (maxgap = 0); promoter-end vs enhancer-end classification
Putative enhancer definition: prior granulosa ATAC-seq peaks overlapped with enhancer-end anchors (ChIPpeakAnno)
Motif enrichment at enhancer classes with HOMER (no parameters or background stated)
Consensus TF binding site construction: ReMap 2022 mm10 ChIP-seq peaks across all tissues merged with BEDTools
TF-occupancy per enhancer class: overlap, percentage, z-score and hierarchical clustering (custom, method unspecified)
ChIP-seq alignment to mm10 with Bowtie2 (no parameters stated)
ChIP-seq peak calling following the MACS2 algorithm, p-value cut-off 1e-10
Differential binding with DiffBind using the DESeq2 linear model, FDR <= 0.05
Genomic distribution of peaks with ChIPseeker (no parameters or annotation source stated)
Gene Ontology enrichment with clusterProfiler (no ontology, universe or cutoff stated)
Signal heatmap generation with deepTools2 (no parameters, normalisation or window stated)
Motif enrichment at AR/GR ChIP-seq peaks with HOMER (no parameters or background stated)
Differential expression of reused public microarray datasets (oviduct, mammary) with NCBI GEO2R at default parameters
Statistical analysis in GraphPad Prism 9 or R: one-way ANOVA; Wilcoxon signed-rank with Benjamini-Hochberg; Pearson correlation; thresholds p <= 0.001 and |mean logFC| >= 0.585
Contact matrix and track visualisation with Juicebox and the UCSC Genome Browser
Mouse husbandry, eCG/hCG superovulation, timed ovary collection and granulosa cell isolation (CBAF1 and Pgr-tm1Bwo lines)
PGRKO genotyping from ear/tail biopsies
RNA extraction, cDNA synthesis and Taqman quantitative real-time PCR
Western blot for AR, GR and beta-actin
Micro-C library construction (Dovetail Micro-C kit) and shallow + deep sequencing
AR, GR and H3K27ac ChIP-seq performed by Active Motif (antibodies #39781, sc-8992, #39133)

gaps.where: whole paper - there is no Code availability section
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked anywhere in the manuscript. No GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage URL appears in the text. Every computational step must be re-implemented from Methods prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Micro-C, enhancer-definition and ChIP-seq analysis scripts in a public repository with a versioned release/DOI and cite it in a Code availability statement.

gaps.missing: Verbatim: "The datasets generated and/or analysed during the current study will be made available upon publication in a peer-reviewed journal." No GEO/SRA/ENA/ArrayExpress/dbGaP/EGA accession is given for the newly generated Micro-C libraries or the AR/GR/H3K27ac ChIP-seq. No sample-to-file mapping is available, so replicate structure (2 biological x 2-3 technical Micro-C libraries; 3-4 ChIP replicates per treatment/genotype) cannot be reconstructed.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit raw and processed Micro-C and ChIP-seq data in GEO/SRA with a sample table mapping each accession to timepoint, genotype and replicate; cite the series accession in the preprint.

gaps.where: C15 (TF occupancy z-score and hierarchical clustering), C13/C22 (HOMER), C19-C21
gaps.missing: The bespoke analysis that converts per-TF enhancer-overlap percentages into z-scores and a clustered heatmap is not described beyond its outline (no distance metric, no linkage method, no normalisation) and no script is provided.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the R/python script that computes the occupancy matrix, the z-score and the clustering, including the clustering call with its arguments.

gaps.where: C14-C15 consensus TF binding site set
gaps.missing: The merged non-redundant per-TF consensus binding site set derived from ReMap 2022 across all mouse tissues is a derived custom database; it is not deposited and the BEDTools merge invocation is not given.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the consensus BED files (or the script plus the exact ReMap download URL) alongside the paper.

gaps.missing: 2a - no version number is given for any bioinformatics tool: FastQC, BWA-MEM, pairtools, Juicertools, Juicebox, HICCUPS/HICCUPSdiff/Arrowhead (Juicer suite), CALDER, biomaRt, ChIPpeakAnno, HOMER, BEDTools, Bowtie2, MACS2, DiffBind, DESeq2, ChIPseeker, clusterProfiler, deepTools2, GEO2R. Names such as MACS2, Bowtie2 and deepTools2 carry a major version in the tool name only, which is not a pin. The R version is not stated; only GraphPad Prism 9 carries an exact version. Version axis therefore scores 1/floating for 24 of 25 C-steps (2b floating-version-lower-bound).
gaps.how_to_close: State exact tool versions in Methods and ship an environment lock (conda-lock / renv.lock / container digest) with the code.

gaps.missing: External reference resources are named but not pinned for retrieval: the Ensembl/biomaRt release used for mm10 TSS coordinates is not stated; the ReMap 2022 download URL/file and the tissue set actually retrieved are not stated; the mm10 assembly source and index build are not stated (no checksum); reused GEO datasets are listed only in Supplementary Table 1, which is outside the assessed text. Under the Delta-B taxonomy these would be prose-DOI-only at best (class B) but cannot be classified at stage 1 without code.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the Ensembl release, the exact ReMap 2022 file URL with checksum, the mm10 FASTA source, and put GEO accessions in the main-text Data availability section.

gaps.missing: Two sub-pipelines are externalised to vendors and not versioned or linked: "Data analysis followed the Dovetail Genomics Micro-C pipeline" and ChIP-seq "was performed by Active Motif ... Peak calling from read count followed the algorithm for MACS2". The vendor pipeline version, its wrapper scripts and any vendor-specific defaults are unavailable, so the described steps are an approximation of what was actually run.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the vendor pipeline version/commit and release the wrapper actually executed, or re-run and document an in-house equivalent.

gaps.missing: GraphPad Prism 9 is commercial software; the split of which tests were run in Prism versus in R is not stated, so part of the statistical path is behind a paid, GUI-only dependency (license-gated, version capped at 1).
gaps.how_to_close: Re-express the reported tests as R/python scripts, or state precisely which figure panels were computed in Prism.

gaps.missing: Six wet-lab steps (mouse husbandry and superovulation, genotyping, qPCR, western blot, Micro-C library prep, vendor ChIP-seq) are non-computational and excluded from |S|. They are the origin of every primary dataset, so computational coverage is 25/31 (81%).
gaps.how_to_close: Not applicable - out of scope for Tier-1 computational assessment.
